sentences.text: In one night, Beyoncé became the most-awarded artist in Grammy history.
The old record: thirty-one, set by conductor Georg Solti.
Half an hour in, Cuff It tied the record.
Her fourth win, for Renaissance, broke it.
Thirty-two Grammys, and a new record.
On stage, she said she was just trying to receive the night.

claims.claim: At the 65th Grammy Awards, Beyoncé won her fourth award of the year, for a career total of 32, the most Grammys of any artist in the awards' history.
claims.excerpt: she won her fourth award of the year for a total of 32 in her career, shattering the record for the most Grammys of any artist in the prize’s 65-year history.
claims.context: Reported 6 February 2023. The total has since been reported differently elsewhere; this video states only the figure at that ceremony.

claims.claim: The record-setting win was best dance/electronic music album, for RENAISSANCE.
claims.excerpt: She had nine nominations this year, and hit the new record just after 7 p.m. PT, when she won best electronic/dance music album.
claims.context: Category wording as given in the report.

claims.claim: Beyoncé had nine nominations at that ceremony.
claims.excerpt: She had nine nominations this year

claims.claim: Beyoncé cried on taking the stage and said, "I'm just trying to receive this night."
claims.excerpt: She cried upon taking the stage, saying, “I’m just trying to receive this night.”
claims.context: A quotation as reported by KQED.

claims.claim: The previous Grammy record of 31 wins was set by the late Hungarian-born classical conductor Georg Solti.
claims.excerpt: The previous Grammy record of 31 wins was a feat set by the late Hungarian-born classical conductor Georg Solti.

claims.claim: Half an hour into the show, Beyoncé tied the all-time record for most Grammys when she and co-writers won best R&B song for Cuff It.
